## Question

Do the agreed product and architecture decisions, reviewed clickable prototype and explicit scope boundaries form a consistent design contract, with runtime feasibility explicitly unproven?

The creator confirmed that this map produces decisions. Implementation and validation are separate work and are not prerequisites for closing the design map. The [decision audit and creator-approved completion boundary](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/22#issuecomment-6478721978) supersede the historical requirement for a full runtime pass before final design approval. No accepted product, safeguard or validation requirement is waived.

## Review contract

Review the accepted resolutions as one contract: permanent Agents navigation, independent project tabs and Project Chats; exact home/provider/session/chat identity; independent provider execution; project/host lifecycle and truthful safeguards; authenticated identity and lifetime boundaries; recovery/disposal; fresh-app opening/restoration; command/profile/focus behavior; and platform/remote/capacity constraints.

The audit links each owning resolution, all ten accepted architecture/refinement resolutions, observable acceptance scenarios, explicit precedence and deliberate exclusions. Detail remains in those resolutions rather than a second copied specification. Existing editor and Agents interiors remain the baseline; runtime implementation choices are not promoted into new product decisions without a demonstrated conflict.

## Profile-target clarification

An exact workspace/environment is already open with profile A. An explicit launch request asks for the same workspace with profile B. Should it reuse that tab and apply profile B through the project-scoped profile-change safeguards?

Recommendation: yes. Reuse the tab, honour the requested profile through existing safeguards, and keep any required restart/reload confined to that project. A cancelled change retains the original tab/profile and reports non-completion. Do not silently ignore the explicit profile, open a duplicate, change the shell/neighbours or queue an automatic retry. Preserve the independent-agent lifetime and permissions already agreed. The [resolution comment](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/22#issuecomment-6478807512) records the creator's approved answer and final design approval.

## Resolution rule

Obtain the creator's answer to the clarification and final approval of the audited design contract. Record the actual answer as the resolution comment, link it from the map's Decisions so far and close the completed map when no decision remains. Approval means design agreement; BrowserWindow plus retained WebContentsViews remains provisional and runtime feasibility remains unproven. It authorizes no production merge or automatic execution.

[Complete the disposable retained-view hosting integration](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/34) and [Validate retained-view hosting against the full accepted contract](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/35) remain open outside this map. The full validation requirements, necessary integration dependency, runtime evidence and separate live runtime verdict remain required for runtime acceptance. The prior experiment verdict is [incomplete with scoped repair evidence](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/33#issuecomment-6478428043). No Stage 1 or overall feasibility pass is recorded. Provider sign-in/work remains deferred and authorization probes remain paused.

## Decision audit — one profile-target clarification remains

### Creator-approved completion boundary

The creator explicitly confirmed in the live conversation: “Yes, keep implementation and validation separate. Verify the agreed decisions for gaps or contradictions so we can finish the map, with runtime feasibility explicitly unproven.”

Accordingly, this ticket now reviews agreement and consistency of the product/architecture contract. Successful runtime validation is not a prerequisite for closing the decision map. This supersedes historical statements making final design approval depend on a complete implementation or runtime feasibility pass. It does not waive a requirement, certify feasibility, authorize a production merge, launch implementation/validation, lift the provider-sign-in deferral, or resume paused authorization probes.

The [implementation backlog](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/34) and [full validation contract](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/35) stay open and separate. The latter remains blocked by necessary integration and still requires its evidence and separate live runtime verdict. The accepted experiment verdict is [retain the candidate provisionally; incomplete with scoped repair evidence](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/33#issuecomment-6478428043).

### Audit coverage and result

Reviewed the original confirmed map notes, the accepted chat, lifecycle, hosting, prototype and fresh-app resolutions, all ten accepted hosting/refinement resolutions, and the accumulated experiment verdicts. Historical implementation failures are evidence of uncompleted work, not additional unsettled product choices. An independent read-only review cross-checked the same ownership/lifecycle contracts.

| Contract area | Consistency finding and observable acceptance scenario | Owning decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Navigation composition | Permanent Agents entry, independent project tabs, and project Chats opening as central chat editors agree with the creator-reviewed prototype. Existing editor/Agents interiors remain the baseline. | [Validate the project tabs and Chats interaction in a prototype](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/21#issuecomment-6464329809) |
| Home and exact-chat identity | Workspace-file/folder plus environment, explicit worktree identity and per-chat home agree across discovery, navigation and reopening. Selecting a chat must return to that exact home/chat, never a similar repository or the session's default chat. | [Define project ownership and navigation for chats](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/17#issuecomment-6456724688) |
| Conversation and execution ownership | Agents and project editors present the provider's same conversation. Closing a project tears down project resources while independently owned agent tools/approval observation continue. Keeping the entire closed workbench alive does not satisfy closure. No duplicate transcript, send, execution claim or approval is authorized by navigation. | [Choose how independent project workbenches share one window](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/20#issuecomment-6464249932), [Define project tab lifecycle and background activity](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/18#issuecomment-6464014913) |
| Tab and app lifecycle | Inactive projects remain live. Genuine project safeguards govern Close/reload; active Close chooses right neighbour, then left, then Agents. Inactive Close retains selection. Whole-window Close/quit coordinates all workbenches; it is distinct from project-tab Close. Agent survival after app quit is not promised. | [Define project tab lifecycle and background activity](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/18#issuecomment-6464014913), [creator-clarified whole-window Close evidence](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/blob/d6f73d25b56/prototypes/live-hosting/product-close/README.md) |
| Identity and native boundaries | Native host, logical workbench, durable workspace, document and connection lifetime remain distinct. Main-established caller/role/target ownership governs dispatch, events, replies and ports. Selection routes native commands; it never authenticates background requests. | [Authenticated native-service boundary](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/20#issuecomment-6465039246), [main-owned generations](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/20#issuecomment-6465585830) |
| Cleanup versus revocation | The later refinement makes ordering precise: legitimate outgoing cleanup and final acknowledgement precede revocation, which precedes replacement/destruction. Crash/unexpected expiry revokes immediately and interrupts pending work. A veto preserves current authority. These are compatible cases, not conflicting rules. | [Direct lifecycle reply ownership and shutdown ordering](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/20#issuecomment-6467262466) |
| Recovery, pending Close and interruption | Project recovery has no intentional collateral teardown. A queued project Close survives a genuine host veto and keeps recovery cancelled. An interrupted Close has a truthful terminal outcome and requires a later explicit action. Late readiness never silently retries it. | [Recovery ownership](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/20#issuecomment-6468194501), [Close precedence](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/20#issuecomment-6469371482), [interrupted Close](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/20#issuecomment-6472391786), [exact-document readiness](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/20#issuecomment-6473367697) |
| Disposal and shared outcome | Every caller joining one Close attempt observes the same real outcome after required teardown/bookkeeping. Registry removal or an already-destroyed view is not success. Later explicit cleanup does not repeat completed phases or revive stale authority. | [Safe project disposal](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/20#issuecomment-6470438779), [one authoritative Close outcome](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/20#issuecomment-6471211872) |
| Fresh app, restoration and discovery | No legacy app-state import; provider-owned history may still be discovered. Restore this app's own permitted tab set/order/selection and recoverable state without replay. Unavailable exact targets remain identifiable with explicit recovery; never substitute another environment/worktree. This explicitly supersedes the early migration assumption. | [Define fresh-app startup, opening and recovery behavior](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/24#issuecomment-6464720430) |
| Commands, profiles and launch arguments | Selected-project command scope, explicit targets from Agents, shared profile settings, stable shell profile, file/line/diff/merge and file/workbench-scoped `--wait` are consistent. One explicit-profile/reuse combination needs the ordering below. | [Define project tab lifecycle and background activity](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/18#issuecomment-6464014913), [Define fresh-app startup, opening and recovery behavior](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/24#issuecomment-6464720430) |
| Keyboard, platforms, remotes and capacity | Keyboard/focus/IME/hidden-view accessibility, macOS/Windows/Linux design and distinct SSH/Dev Container authority remain requirements. No custom shortcut scheme was selected; none is introduced by this audit. Roughly 200 ms warm switching and 3–5/ten-project workloads are unmeasured goals; no resource budget, suspension policy, provider-wide or process-isolation proof is inferred. | [Original confirmed scope](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/16#issuecomment-6478313900), [hosting ownership](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/20#issuecomment-6464249932), [lifecycle/capacity](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/18#issuecomment-6464014913) |

### One precise remaining design question

**When workspace App is already open with profile A and an explicit launch request opens that exact workspace/environment with profile B, should it reuse that tab and apply the requested profile through the project-scoped profile-switch safeguards?**

Recommendation: **yes**. Reuse the exact existing tab and apply profile B to that project through the established profile-change flow. Run any required restart/reload safeguards only for that project. A cancelled change leaves the original tab/profile usable and reports the request as not completed; do not silently ignore the explicit profile, create a duplicate tab, change the shell/neighbours, or queue an automatic retry. Any independent agent work retains its already agreed lifetime and permissions.

Why this is a decision gap: the accepted rules separately require exact-workspace reuse and preservation of explicit launch profiles, but do not state their combined ordering. The source is not a sufficient answer: in read-only checkout `fb20a73421587048583fbbeb74e2fefaa255eba6`, `windowsMainService.ts` reuses an existing workspace through `doOpenFilesInExistingWindow`, whose request does not carry `forceProfile`; profile resolution is in the separate load path. `userDataProfileManagement.ts` provides project profile switching, extension-host cancellation and remote reload handling. Those are integration facts, not evidence that this launch combination already satisfies the intended contract.

All other reviewed contract areas have an accepted rule, an explicit later refinement, or a deliberate scope/validation boundary. No additional architecture choice is established by missing adapters or unperformed checks.

### Pending resolution

This is an audit and proposed final clarification, not a creator answer. Keep this ticket and the map open until the creator answers the profile question and approves the audited design contract. On approval, record the actual answer here as the final decision-only resolution, link it from the map, and close the completed map. Runtime feasibility remains explicitly unproven and the separate implementation/validation issues remain open.

No implementation, build, runtime test, credential request or authorization probe was performed in this review.

## Resolution — audited design approved; runtime feasibility unproven

The creator explicitly approved the final clarification and audited design in the live conversation:

> Yes, approve that clarification and the audited design.

This resolves final **design approval** under the creator's decision-only map boundary. The [decision audit](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/22#issuecomment-6478721978) indexes the accepted product/architecture contract, all ten accepted hosting/refinement resolutions, observable acceptance scenarios, precedence and scope boundaries. Those owning resolutions remain authoritative; this approval does not copy or replace them with a second specification.

### Final profile-target clarification

When an explicit launch request opens an exact workspace/environment already open under profile A but requests profile B:

- Reuse that workspace's existing project tab and apply the requested profile through the project-scoped profile-change safeguards.
- Confine any required restart/reload to that project. Preserve the already accepted independent-agent lifetime, execution ownership and permissions; the shell and neighbouring projects retain their own state/profile.
- If the change is cancelled, preserve the original tab/profile and report the request as not completed. Do not silently ignore the explicit profile, create a duplicate project tab, or queue an automatic retry.

This settles the only unspecified combination found in the audit: exact-workspace reuse and explicit-profile preservation now have an agreed ordering. It is a design requirement, not a claim that the current launch/profile integration implements it.

### Approved contract and completion

The audit found no other unresolved design gap or contradiction among the accepted navigation, home/provider/session/exact-chat identity, conversation/execution ownership, project/host lifecycle, authenticated native boundaries, generations/revocation, recovery, disposal/shared outcomes, readiness, fresh-app startup/opening/restoration, command/profile scope, keyboard/focus, platform/remote and capacity requirements.

The creator-reviewed [clickable navigation prototype](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/21#issuecomment-6464329809) remains the accepted interaction composition. Later lifecycle refinements clarify the original rules; fresh-app/no-import supersedes migration assumptions, and this decision-only completion boundary supersedes historical requirements that full runtime validation block final design approval. Deliberate exclusions and all product/safeguard requirements remain as audited.

The decision map can now close: no in-scope design question or fog remains. BrowserWindow with retained WebContentsViews remains a **provisional candidate**, and **runtime feasibility is explicitly unproven**. This is not a Stage 1 pass, overall feasibility pass, runtime acceptance verdict, production merge authorization or instruction to launch further execution.

### Separate implementation and validation

- [Complete the disposable retained-view hosting integration](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/34) remains open for missing integration against the accepted contracts, including the profile-target clarification above.
- [Validate retained-view hosting against the full accepted contract](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/35) remains open and natively blocked by necessary implementation. Its entire inherited contract, exact-source evidence, failure accounting and separate live creator runtime verdict remain required. Design approval waives none of them.
- The [accumulated experiment verdict](https://github.com/ejjsharpe/escode/issues/33#issuecomment-6478428043) remains incomplete with scoped repair evidence. Provider/tool/approval continuity after actual project closure, native usability/resource cost and platform/remote compatibility retain their explicit unproven status.
- Provider sign-in/work remains deferred and authorization probes remain paused. Future execution may return a demonstrated incompatibility or real trade-off as a precise new decision effort; missing code or an unrun test alone does not reopen the agreed design.

No implementation or runtime tests were performed in this decision review.
